text:
Jordan: heads-up — ran into a throttling surprise during a demo. Onboarding org had lots of tiny bursts (~50 reqs in 1s) and our token-bucket cut them hard even though their 1m avg is under quota. not ideal for demo or bursty mobile traffic

Lei: saw the same traces. the token refill interval is too coarse for sub-second bursts. token-bucket gives predictable steady-state but punishes microbursts. thinking hybrid leaky+token or a short grace "ephemeral" bucket that can absorb spikes without touching long-term budget

Claire: proposal sketch — ephemeral credit escrow per-key that refills quickly but drains from a budget with different accounting. basically: two layers: short-window fast-bucket (5s) + long-window reserve (1h). short wins for latency, long enforces cost. examples: 
```yaml
quota_scheme: hybrid_h2
short_window_ms: 5000
short_capacity: 120
long_window_s: 3600
long_capacity: 10000
charge_mode: amortized
```

Jordan: i like amortized charging — means demos don't blow through monthly quotas instantly. but need clear console UX so customers understand transient boosts vs real usage. also need to avoid gaming (someone could burst constantly and slowly bleed budget)

Mike: telemetry to add: gauge burst_reserve_{org,key}, histogram microburst_size_ms, counter ephemeral_topups. need to tie to traces so we can see which route consumed ephemeral credits. also emit events when ephemeral pool exhausted: `ephemeral_exhausted` with org_id and hint

Lei: on fairness: hierarchical token buckets with priority weights might help — SLA tiers get first dibs on short pool. fallback policy: if short_pool empty, try queued requests for up to 200ms, else fallback to cheaper model or 429 depending on route config

Claire: UX ideas for console: "Burst reserve" widget per-org (sparkline of reserve level), a toggle to enable/disable ephemeral boosts, and an "Emergency top-up" button for Dedicated. show predicted burn-through at current spike rate. tiny mock: Burst reserve: [████▁▁▁] 28/120 (5s window) 

sre-bot: deploy-notice — rate-limiter v3.14 staged to canaries (10% orgs) at 2024-04-05T15:00Z. will log `burst_policy_decision` for every throttled request.

Jordan: canary plan — enable ephemeral pool for 10% of orgs, split 50/50 between SLA and non-SLA, run 48h, watch eviction rate, latency tail, and cost delta. if cost delta > 5% escalate.

Mike: quick config snippet for canary: 
```json
{
  "canary": {"percent": 10},
  "policy": {"short_window_ms": 5000, "short_capacity": 150, "priority_buckets": ["sla","standard"]}
}
```

Lei: on enforcement internals — prefer keeping short-window operations in fast-path in-memory ring buffer to avoid datastore roundtrips. long-window accounting can be async and eventually consistent. this keeps p50/p95 latency stable under burst.

Claire: edge-case: multi-route fanout (one parent request fans out to 5 model calls) — need aggregate pre-check so ephemeral pool considers total fanout tokens, otherwise one request can wipe reserve. Suggest a preflight cost estimate API: `POST /quota/preflight {cost: 5}` -> reserved 5 short tokens atomically

Jordan: action items: (1) implement short-window in-memory pool + preflight API, (2) add telemetry metrics and console widgets, (3) craft canary rollout + AB config, (4) add docs on accounting semantics (amortized vs eager charging). I'll own (3) and docs. Claire take console + preflight UX. Lei/infra do implementation. Mike add telemetry dashboard charts.

claire: :thumbsup: will draft console mocks and a short copy explaining burst vs steady usage.

mike: putting dashboard panels on the spike-ops grafana board. will add alerts: ephemeral_exhausted_rate > 1/min for 5m => page oncall.

sre-bot: noted. scheduled canary window and will post roll metrics to #eng-sre.

Jordan: thanks — let's sync tomorrow 10am to finalize canary gating thresholds. keep discussion here for small updates only.
